html:
Fulbert Youlou was a Catholic priest who became the first president of the Republic of the Congo at independence in 1960, and was overthrown in 1963.

A Lari from the Pool region, he built his following among the believers of André Matsoua, and his election as mayor of Brazzaville in 1956 began his rise. Clashes between his supporters and rivals in 1959 left many dead.

As president he was close to France and to Moise Tshombe in Katanga, and he planned a one-party state. In August 1963 three days of strikes and protests by trade unions and the youth, the Trois Glorieuses, forced him to resign. The radical regime that followed led toward the People's Republic of 1969.
